In other parts of Europe, the unemployment rate in Hungary rose to 4.8% in June to August. Hungary's current account swung to a €0.25B deficit in Q2.
Retail sales in Denmark grew by 3.7% Y/Y in August.
Producer prices in Sweden increased 6.8% Y/Y in August.
The annual growth rate of lending to Swedish households held at 3.3% in August.
Germany's GfK Consumer Climate Indicator fell to -30.6 heading into October.

edged 0.68% higher to 640.7, as easing oil prices and a pause in the global bond selloff eased pressure on investors. European natural gas prices dropped below €74 per megawatt-hour on Friday. Gold traded around $4,270 an ounce on Friday and was on track to decline more than 2% for the week.
The euro ended the week below the $1.14 threshold, marking its weakest level in two months as the U.S. dollar
remained supported by growing expectations of further Federal Reserve.
In the bond market, the U.S. bond was up 1 basis point to 5.17%.
UK's 10-year yield was down 3 basis points to 5.36%.
Germany's 10-year yield was down 2 basis points to 3.59%.
